license: Not verified (not run). SAM2 checkpoints are under Meta's SAM licence; the samesh repo's own licence was not audited because the candidate was not run.
outcome: NOT RUN - by the bake-off's own gating rule: 'SAMesh or another SAM2-lifting approach - only if 1 and 2 are quick fails; it is the heaviest pipeline.' Candidates 1 (P3-SAM) and 2 (PartField) both installed and produced scored segmentations on both proof meshes, so the condition for attempting SAMesh never triggered.
paper_notes: Upstream: https://github.com/gtangg12/samesh - zero-shot; renders multiview modalities (normals / shape-diameter), runs SAM2 automatic masks per view, then lifts and associates masks into a 3D part segmentation.

Upstream tested on Python 3.12 + CUDA 11.8; requires a separately downloaded SAM2 checkpoint and building SAM2 (README warns to use --no-build-isolation on build issues). No Windows evidence in the repo.

It is the heaviest of the three pipelines (a full multiview render + SAM2 inference + mask-association stack, vs a single feed-forward pass for P3-SAM/PartField), and its quality on fused organic bipeds/quadrupeds is unproven here.
If a future slice wants a third opinion, SAMesh is the candidate to try - budget it as its own slice, not a fallback afternoon.
